html:
The Djabugay, also written Tjapukai, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the rainforest around today's Kuranda, in the hills above Cairns in far north Queensland, along the Barron River.

Their neighbours were the Yidinji to the south, the Dyirbal and Mbabaram inland and the Kuku Yalanji to the north. The rainforest gave them nuts, fruits, game and fish, and its toxic seeds were made edible by leaching.

The railway up the Barron Gorge to Kuranda opened in 1891 to serve the tin and gold fields inland. In the 1980s a Djabugay dance theatre at Kuranda, later a large cultural park near Cairns, brought their songs and dances to many visitors.
sum: The Djabugay, also written Tjapukai, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the rainforest around today's Kuranda, in the hills above Cairns in far north Queensland, along the Barron River.
